items.observed: The first frozen RC1 setup defined a custody receipt schema but did not freeze the execution-time checker that would validate a real receipt and returned profile artifacts.
items.risk: Allowing the checker to be invented after writer output would weaken the meaning of the prerequisite result.
items.correction: Before any writer invocation or semantic exposure, preserve the first candidate in Git history, add a frozen execution checker, pin the writer model/digest/destination, tighten machine-readable profile config requirements, and issue a new setup closure.

items.observed: The second frozen setup still left exact writer request options and request construction to the executor rather than freezing the launcher/transport.
items.risk: Executor discretion over request parameters or source packing would add an avoidable controlled-variable and custody ambiguity.
items.correction: Before any writer invocation or semantic exposure, preserve the second candidate in Git history, freeze the RC0 request options and a five-file response schema in WRITER-TRANSPORT.json, and add frozen run_writer.py as the sole authorized launcher/custodian.

items.observed: Review of the third setup found that the checker searched the whole allowed prompt for forbidden filenames, even though BOOTSTRAP-MANIFEST.json legitimately contains those names in its denylist.
items.risk: A valid writer request would be falsely classified as contaminated.
items.correction: Before any writer invocation or semantic exposure, preserve the third candidate in Git history, replace string scanning with exact structural parsing of the writer prompt/source bundle, and add a setup self-test that exercises the frozen prompt/request builder.
